title: Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained as to the BCO 15-3 specification: NP erred by dividing the JC verdict and amending the JC's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; BCO 15-3 required NP to approve or disapprove the JC's judgment as a whole without debate. Specifications of error arising from the investigation, indictment, evidence, and trial procedures were not sustained because Bachmann's unconditional post-trial confession waived them. SJC rendered the decision that should have been rendered: the JC's judgment (Not Guilty to Charge A; Guilty to Charge B) and censure of Admonition became the SJC's judgment; case remanded to NP; Moderator to deliver admonition; Appellant restored to good standing, subject to NP possibly requiring items 2–4 of pastoral counsel/oversight; item 1 moot.
first_summary: Bachmann, a teaching elder, appealed after Nashville Presbytery replaced his judicial commission's recommended admonition with indefinite suspension. The SJC sustained the appeal, finding Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the censure, and rendered the commission's judgment and admonition as the decision. The case was remanded to Presbytery.
summary: TE James Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to replace his judicial commission's recommended admonition with indefinite suspension. The SJC sustained the appeal: Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the verdict and amending the censure, which it had to approve or disapprove as a whole without debate. Bachmann's earlier procedural challenges were not sustained; his unconditional post-trial confession waived them. The SJC rendered the commission's judgment and admonition as its own decision, remanded to Presbytery, and restored Bachmann to good standing, subject to possible pastoral oversight items 2–4.

The SJC issued the decision on appeal in Case 2016-15 at the 46th GA (2018); the panel heard the appeal on 5/2/17, and the written decision was approved unanimously by the panel and by the SJC, with concurrences, one disqualification, and one recusal.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 17–53, 63–73. After a JC trial and Bachmann's post-trial confession, NP divided the verdict and replaced the JC's recommended admonition with indefinite suspension; Bachmann appealed, and the issue was whether NP erred in amending and approving the amended JC judgment.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 75–77, 81–127, 129–177, 181–201. Specifications A (investigation, indictment, evidence, trial procedures) were not sustained because the unconditional post-trial confession waived them; the BCO 15-3 specification was sustained because NP debated, divided, and amended the JC judgment/censure; SJC rendered the JC judgment and censure and remanded.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 92–121, 135–158, 189–201, 205. The SJC distinguished post-trial confession from BCO 38-1 provisional/negotiated confession and found no plea agreement in the record; restoration to good standing permits NP to require items 2–4 of pastoral counsel/oversight; item 1 is moot; concurrence, disqualification, and recusal noted.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 51–53, 177, 201. The SJC incorporated/rendered the JC's September 6, 2016 judgment and recommended censure of admonition as the Commission's judgment; no separate incorporated decision is missing from the supplied source.
